note: Review proposals, not production corrections. Nothing here modifies imported documents or database rows, and no runtime code loads this file. Each proposal covers one field of one source; accepting one does not upgrade capabilities or apply to other entries or sources. Evidence references carry sha256 hashes of the exact stored values; the builder resolves them into the ignored enrichment_fixtures files.
attribution: AI-assisted review; pending owner acceptance; not independently human-verified or culinarily validated.

proposals.title: Stored ingredient name includes a quantity fragment
abstentions: amount, unit and quantity_text stay unchanged: the original line reads "1- cup", and the trailing hyphen may mark a truncated range, so neither a single amount nor a confirmed unit follows from it.
ing-1, ing-3, ing-14, ing-15 and ing-16 have similar name problems; each would need its own review and is not covered here.
establishes: The source line names the ingredient "coconut milk", and step-4 adds coconut milk.
The stored name "- cup coconut milk" carries a quantity fragment that is not part of the ingredient name.
does_not_establish: How much coconut milk ("1-" may be a truncated range).
That the stored unit should become "cup"; the unit field stays as stored until the quantity is reviewed.
Anything about other ingredients or other foodie sources with similar parse artifacts.
proposals.scope: This one field of this one source.
proposals.effect_if_accepted: Only the displayed and matched name changes. Rendering already shows the intact original line; recommendability and capabilities are unaffected.

proposals.title: Quantity without a unit must stay unknown

No amount is re-parsed: the stored amount is the string "3", which the renderer already shows as an unknown amount with quantity text "3".
The other five 000250 quantities have the same missing-unit problem and are not covered by this entry.
establishes: The source gives nam pla the bare quantity "3" (third raw quantity value) with no unit anywhere in the record.
Step-0 uses nam pla without an amount; the row is flagged units_unknown.
does_not_establish: The unit, and therefore how much nam pla to use.
Whether "3" is a count, a volume or something else.
proposals.scope: This one field of this one source. It remains unknown; the proposal is an explicit abstention.

proposals.title: FOLLOWUP-01: steps use ingredients the ingredient list omits

issue.message: Steps 1-3 use potatoes, oil and water; the ingredient list does not name them.

abstentions: No ingredient entries are added for potatoes, oil or water.
No quantity or unit is assigned to any ingredient, listed or missing.
The raw quantity values are not aligned to names: 9 values for 6 names cannot be mapped reliably.
The water range "1/2 to 3/4 cup" stays in step-3 text; it is not promoted to an ingredient amount.
establishes: Steps 1-3 use potatoes, oil and water.
None of the six listed ingredient names is potatoes, oil or water.
The raw quantity list has 9 values for 6 names (flag ingredient_quantity_mismatch). That is consistent with entries missing from the name list, but does not prove it.
does_not_establish: How many potatoes or how much oil; the kind of oil.
Which raw quantity value belongs to which ingredient, including whether "1/2" is the water.
That the source is unusable as a discovery pointer; it only cannot be presented as ready to cook.
Anything about other sources with an ingredient_quantity_mismatch flag.
proposals.scope: This one source. Not a rule for other rows, and not an automatic detector.
proposals.effect_if_accepted: Recording this issue on the row (a separate, authorized data change, not made here) would make the existing gate treat it as not recommendable: it would be kept out of model evidence and shown only as a discovery pointer with why = "blocking source defect". tests/test_recommendations_source_consistency.py shows this with an isolated fixture. The stored row is unchanged today and is still presentable.
